units: NZD per share unless stated; net assets in millions
method: NAV-per-share compounding with exit price-to-NAV (discount) multiple, plus explicit valuation of the distribution stream. NOT an FCF DCF.
valuation_philosophy: Barramundi is a closed-end NZX-listed investment company (LIC), not an operating business: it holds a concentrated portfolio of ~25-35 Australian-listed (predominantly ASX) equities managed by Fisher Funds, has no revenue, no EBITDA, no capex, no SBC, and zero total debt in every reported period. Reported NetIncome is dominated by unrealised/realised mark-to-market swings on the portfolio (from -$34.6m in FY2022 to +$52.3m in FY2021) and is pure noise as a growth driver - EPS CAGR, revenue CAGR and FCF CAGR are NOT computed or used anywhere in this model. A conventional FCF/WACC/Gordon-growth DCF is invalid here and has not been used; this model instead follows the NAV-compounding + exit-discount framework already applied to AFI.NZ, BIT.NZ and BIF.NZ in this research folder: (1) start from a CURRENT (not stale audited) NAV per share; (2) project NAV per share forward using a component build of gross portfolio return, less manager alpha (currently negative given persistent underperformance), less fees, less a recurring warrant-dilution drag, less the 8% p.a. distribution policy; (3) separately value the distribution stream the shareholder actually receives as cash (the 8% payout is NOT lost value even though it shrinks NAV per share - it is realised, spendable income and must be added back at the shareholder level); (4) apply a scenario exit discount/premium to the year-5 NAV, since the market-clearing valuation metric for an LIC is price/NAV, not an earnings multiple; (5) discount both the interim dividend stream and the terminal exit value at a small-cap, AUD-exposed cost of equity. THE CENTRAL, HONEST CONCLUSION: this is an income-plus-discount-closing vehicle, not a growth compounder. The 8% p.a. distribution policy (2% of average NAV per quarter) is set independently of the portfolio's actual total return (the portfolio's organic dividend yield is only ~2%), so in any year where total return falls short of 8% - which has been true recently (FY2025 adjusted NAV return +3.9%, H1 FY2026 -6.6%, both against a materially higher benchmark) - the distribution is substantially a RETURN OF SHAREHOLDERS' OWN CAPITAL, not distributed profit, and it mechanically erodes NAV per share over time. This is not a modelling assumption; it is the observed 8-year record: NAV per share was $0.71 at FY2018 and has fallen to roughly $0.54 today (a ~-3.3% p.a. per-share CAGR over that period) despite a rising Australian equity market, because distributions have persistently exceeded organic total return. The fee load (1.25% base management fee, stepping down only when the Manager underperforms, plus a 10%-of-excess-return performance fee above a demanding hurdle) is a further permanent drag layered on top. The realistic source of return here is therefore: (a) the underlying Australian equity market's own long-run return, net of a manager that has recently, materially underperformed its benchmark and is assumed in the base case to continue doing so modestly; (b) the cash distribution stream, which is real value even though NAV-dilutive; and (c) whatever narrowing (or widening) occurs in the market's current ~11-13% discount to NAV, against a Board buyback trigger of 6% that provides only a partial floor. The base case in this model produces an intrinsic value BELOW the current market price, and that conclusion is reported honestly rather than engineered toward an upside case - the current market discount is not obviously excessive once a flat-to-mildly-declining NAV-per-share trajectory and a persisting fee/underperformance drag are correctly priced in.

inputs.nav_current_basis_source: Mean of two disclosed undiluted NAV observations from the Analysis JSON: $0.5312 at 22-Jul-2026 and $0.5442 at 29-Jul-2026, averaged to $0.5377 and rounded to $0.5375 per explicit instruction. Used in preference to the stale 31-Dec-2025 audited NAV ($0.6328) because the portfolio has materially declined since then (H1 FY2026 alone was a $15.4m net loss / -6.6% adjusted NAV return) and the late-July 2026 figures are the most current disclosed marks.
inputs.nav_decline_note: NAV per share has fallen from $0.71 (undiluted, 30-Jun-2025) to approximately $0.5375 (late-Jul-2026) in just over a year - a combination of a weak H1 FY2026 portfolio return (-6.6% adjusted NAV return vs benchmark +5.6%) and the ongoing 8% p.a. distribution policy paid out of a materially smaller total return.
inputs.shares_asof: 2025-12-31 (H1 FY2026, last reported count; no evidence of a share count change since other than ongoing buybacks, which if executed would modestly reduce this)
inputs.net_debt_treatment_note: Total debt is zero in every reported period (a genuine, disclosed fact - this is an unleveraged closed-end equity fund). Cash is already fully embedded inside NAV per share, so it is not added again separately; net_debt is set to 0 for schema purposes rather than a negative net-cash figure, to avoid double-counting cash that is already inside the NAV base.
inputs.warrants_treatment: This tranche (1-for-4, issued Aug-2025) expired 7-Aug-2026, two days before this valuation date, with NAV (~$0.5375-0.6328 over its life) always well below the $0.70 strike. Treated as LAPSED WORTHLESS with zero dilution - no adjustment made to shares outstanding or NAV for this tranche. However, Barramundi issues warrants on a roughly ANNUAL recurring basis (prior Oct-2023 tranche partially exercised at $0.63, raising $31.5m; a new tranche should be expected in the next 12-24 months), and past tranches issued at or below prevailing NAV have been genuinely dilutive to non-participating holders. This recurring pattern is captured as an ongoing ~0.5%/yr (base case) NAV-per-share dilution drag in the projections below, rather than by modelling a specific future tranche.
inputs.revenue: n/a - not an operating company; see valuation_philosophy
inputs.interest_income: not separately adjusted - included within portfolio total return; no meaningful net cash pile outside the equity portfolio to double-count
inputs.sbc_source: unavailable - not applicable; Barramundi is externally managed by Fisher Funds Management Limited (fee-based, no employee equity compensation scheme at the listed entity)
inputs.buyback_cash: not separately disclosed as an annual total in the source data; buybacks are modelled as NAV-accretive within the total-return build rather than as a distinct share-count mechanic
inputs.projected_shares_note: Not separately projected - this is a per-share NAV compounding model; the recurring warrant-issuance dilution risk is captured via the dilution_drag_pct term inside NAV-per-share growth (see assumptions), not via a separate share count path.

management_fee_pct_of_gav.mechanism: steps down 0.1% per 1% of underperformance vs NZ 90-Day Bank Bill Index; currently at the floor due to a 7.4pp H1 FY2026 shortfall, but can step back up if performance recovers

inputs.performance_fee: 10% (plus GST) of excess return above Bank Bill Index + 7% hurdle, capped at 1.25% of adjusted NAV, subject to high-water mark; NOT earned in FY2025 or H1 FY2026
inputs.distribution_policy: 2% of average NAV per quarter (~8% p.a.), standing Board policy since Aug-2009, not tied to actual earned return
inputs.fcf_dcf_note: Not applicable. No revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital or FCF exists for this vehicle - see valuation_philosophy. All standard FCF-DCF schema fields (WACC/Gordon terminal value, SBC adjustment, share dilution mechanic) are replaced by the NAV-compounding equivalents below.

historical_growth.methodology: Barramundi's own relevant value driver is NAV-per-share TOTAL RETURN (NAV growth + distributions paid). Standard revenue/EPS/FCF CAGRs are NOT computed - there is no revenue or FCF concept for this vehicle, and NetIncome/EPS is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (FY2021 NI $52.3m vs FY2022 NI -$34.6m on a similar share base) rather than any operating trend. Using EPS or NetIncome CAGR as a growth driver would be actively misleading.
historical_growth.nav_per_share_cagr_fy18_to_current_note: From audited FY2018 NAV ($0.7074) to the current-basis NAV ($0.5375, late-Jul-2026), a span of ~8.1 years: -3.34% p.a. This plain NAV-per-share decline (BEFORE adding back distributions received) is the clearest evidence that the 8% p.a. distribution policy has substantially exceeded the portfolio's organic total return over a full market cycle. Adding back the distribution stream received over the period would show a materially less negative (likely modestly positive) total return to a holder, but the NAV-per-share base itself has genuinely shrunk.
historical_growth.eps_note: Not computed - EPS/NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio revaluation (FY2021 +$52.3m to FY2022 -$34.6m), not an operating trend. Using an EPS CAGR here would be pure noise, per explicit task instruction.
historical_growth.equity_note: Not used as the growth driver - total shareholders' equity CAGR conflates NAV-per-share performance with share issuance (warrant exercises, DRP) and distributions paid; NAV PER SHARE (above) is the correct per-holder metric for an LIC.
historical_growth.fcf_note: Not applicable - no FCF concept exists for a closed-end investment company; TotalDebt is zero and there is no capex/working-capital cycle.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base_case_implied_nav_per_share_growth (component build: gross portfolio return - manager alpha - fees - dilution drag - distribution payout; see assumptions.base)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Not applicable in the usual sense (no revenue/EPS CAGR exists to diverge from), but flagged: the historical NAV-per-share record (-0.02% to +3.57% CAGR over 5-7yr windows, -3.34% over 8yr to the current basis) is itself highly sensitive to the endpoint chosen (FY2021's $0.8687 was a post-COVID market peak; the current $0.5375 reflects a recent sharp H1 FY2026 drawdown). The base case does not naively extrapolate any single historical window; it is built bottom-up from a gross-return-less-fees-less-distribution framework instead (see assumptions.base rationale).
historical_growth.notes: Do not use EPS CAGR, revenue CAGR or FCF CAGR anywhere in this model - none exist or are meaningful for this vehicle. NAV per share is the only valid per-holder growth metric, and even that must be read alongside the distribution stream (which is real income, not lost value) to assess total shareholder return.

wacc_rationale.methodology: Cost of equity built up from a NZ risk-free rate and an Australian/NZ equity risk premium (since ~91% of assets are AUD-denominated Australian-listed equities), plus additive premiums for small-cap illiquidity and partial/variable AUD currency hedging. This is higher than a large diversified operating company's WACC but is NOT venture-style (unlike BIF.NZ) because the underlying portfolio is a liquid, professionally custodied, dual-audited basket of large/mid-cap ASX-listed names with daily market pricing (Level 1 assets), not Level-3 manager marks.
wacc_rationale.rationale: The equity risk premium is applied against the underlying Australian equity market since that is what NAV actually tracks. The illiquidity premium (+1.5%) reflects Barramundi's own sub-scale market cap (~NZ$166m) and thin secondary trading. The currency premium (+0.75%) reflects that the Manager only partially and variably hedges AUD exposure back to NZD (H1 FY2026 saw a $12.8m loss on forward FX contracts on top of the underlying portfolio loss), so hedging itself is a source of volatility rather than pure risk reduction. Bull/bear cost-of-equity is shifted +/-1.0-1.5pp to reflect scenario-consistent risk (bull: manager alpha recovers, reducing perceived execution risk; bear: continued underperformance and distribution-funded capital erosion raise the effective risk borne by a holder).

base.rationale: Gross portfolio return anchored to a long-run Australian equity nominal total return (~8.5%). Manager alpha assumed mildly NEGATIVE (-0.5%), i.e. the portfolio does not fully recover to matching its benchmark - a skeptical, evidence-led read of a manager that has underperformed by 9.6pp (FY2025) and 12.2pp (H1 FY2026) in its two most recent periods, with the base case assuming only partial normalisation, not a reversal to outperformance. Management fee set at a blended 1.0% (between the 0.75% underperformance floor currently in effect and the 1.25% ceiling that would apply if performance normalises - since a fee cut is explicitly conditional on continued underperformance, assuming the floor persists forever would be inconsistent with also assuming alpha improves). The 8% distribution policy is modelled as continuing unchanged (long-standing Board policy since 2009, no indication of a change), producing a NAV-per-share path that is mildly NEGATIVE (-1.8% p.a.) - consistent with the actual 8-year record of NAV/share declining from $0.71 to ~$0.54. The exit discount narrows modestly from today's ~11-13% to -9%, reflecting the active 6%-trigger buyback programme providing a partial (not full) floor, without assuming full discount closure that the manager's recent performance record does not support.

bull.rationale: Manager alpha turns modestly POSITIVE as the technology/classified-advertising holdings (WiseTech, Xero) recover from the AI-driven derating the Manager itself has characterised as a valuation reset rather than a business-quality change, and the new BHP/Rio Tinto commodity tilt pays off. A sustained positive-alpha period would also let the management fee normalise toward its ceiling less aggressively than the floor scenario (0.85% used, below the 1.25% cap, reflecting continued fee discipline). Active buybacks plus a demonstrated performance recovery narrow the discount close to par.

bear.rationale: Underperformance persists and worsens (a continuation of the H1 FY2026 -6.6% vs +5.6% experience), the fee reverts to its 1.25% ceiling as the underperformance trigger for the reduction lapses (fee floor only applies while currently underperforming; a bear scenario does not imply the floor persists, since the floor mechanism is itself evidence the Manager is doing poorly against a rising benchmark whose bar the fee-reduction clause is measured against, not an absolute cost saving), lower Australian equity returns from currently elevated valuations, and the discount widens toward its historical worst levels as investor confidence in the Manager erodes further, consistent with the ~13% discount already reached by late Jul-2026.

projections.distributions_note: Dividend per share each year = distribution_yield_pct x average of opening and closing NAV for that year (2% per quarter x average NAV, compounded to an annual ~8% policy rate). These distributions are received as real cash by the shareholder and are added back at PV in the valuation below alongside the year-5 exit value - the NAV-per-share erosion they cause is NOT a loss of shareholder value, only a mechanical consequence of returning capital via the NAV base rather than retaining it.

five_year_irr_build_memo.description: Primary valuation build: PV of the 5-year distribution stream plus PV of the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x scenario exit discount), both discounted at the scenario's cost of equity. This is presented as the headline 'valuation' block below (unlike the AFI/BIT convention of using this as a secondary memo), because for BRM the shareholder's total return depends materially on both an already-declining NAV trajectory AND a meaningful distribution stream that a simpler 'current NAV x fair discount' framing would omit.

headline_static_memo.description: Cross-check only (not the primary valuation): current NAV per share ($0.5375) x scenario fair exit discount, with no forward compounding or distribution value added. Shown for consistency with the AFI.NZ/BIT.NZ headline convention.

base.implied_exit_multiple: n/a - LIC valuation uses P/NAV, not an earnings or FCF multiple

valuation.note: terminal_pct_of_value = PV(year-5 exit) / (PV(dividends) + PV(exit)). Unlike an all-distribution-free vehicle (e.g. BIF.NZ, 100% terminal), BRM's ~8% p.a. distribution policy means a genuine 33-43% of the 5-year fair value in every scenario comes from interim cash received, not just the terminal exit - a real, structural difference in the risk profile of this investment versus a non-distributing LIC/VC trust.

entry_price.methodology: Price today such that 5 years of projected base-case distributions plus the year-5 exit value (year-5 NAV x base-case -9% exit discount) discounted at 15% equals that price.
entry_price.memo: A 15% IRR hurdle applied to a vehicle whose base-case total return (before any discount-widening drag, i.e. distribution yield 8% plus NAV growth -1.8% = ~6.2%) sits well below 15% mechanically requires a deep discount to today's price to work as a 15%-IRR entry point (-24.9% from the current $0.48, i.e. buying around $0.36, an implied ~33% discount to the current NAV of $0.5375). This is WIDER than Barramundi's own observed historical P/NAV range (roughly -13% to +13% across FY2018-H1FY2026), so it should be read as 'this is not a realistic 15%-IRR entry level at any price BRM has recently traded at' rather than an achievable near-term target. The more relevant question for a holder is whether the current price (-11% to -13% discount to NAV per the Analysis JSON, or -10.7% to the current-basis NAV used in this model) fairly compensates for the base-case ~6.2% pre-distribution total return outlook and the demonstrated fee/underperformance drag - which this model's base case answers with a modest NEGATIVE expected return (-16.2%) at the cost of equity, not the 15% hurdle.

sanity_check.description: For a closed-end investment company the only valid sanity anchor is price-to-NAV (P/NAV, equivalent to price-to-book since NAV per share IS book value per share for an LIC holding a marked-to-market securities portfolio). P/E and EV/EBITDA are explicitly NOT APPLICABLE and are not computed - NetIncome is dominated by unrealised mark-to-market portfolio swings (FY2021 +$52.3m to FY2022 -$34.6m on a similar share count) with no operating-earnings concept, and there is no EBITDA concept for a portfolio of listed securities with zero debt and zero capex.

implied_multiples.price_to_earnings: n/a - NetIncome is unrealised/realised mark-to-market on the equity portfolio, not an operating earnings concept
implied_multiples.ev_to_ebitda: n/a - no EBITDA concept for a debt-free listed-securities portfolio

sanity_check.historical_pnav_range_note: Estimated by comparing period-end NAV per share (from ShareholdersEquity/SharesOutstanding in the Metrics CSV) against approximate contemporaneous NZX share prices (from 10-year quarterly Yahoo Finance history). FY2022's +12.6% reading is an outlier driven by a sharp NAV decline into 30-Jun-2022 (post rate-shock market drawdown) that the share price had not yet fully caught down to; excluding that outlier the range is roughly -13% (widest discount, both FY2018 and now) to +1.3% (narrowest, FY2021 - near the market peak). All three DCF scenarios (bear -16%, base -9%, bull -2%) sit within or close to this observed range and do not require adjustment.
sanity_check.diagnosis: The base-case intrinsic value ($0.40) sits BELOW the current market price ($0.48), which at first glance looks unusual for a 'sanity check pass', but this is the direct and honest consequence of (a) starting from a current NAV of $0.5375 that is already ~10.7% below the current price on a like-for-like basis is NOT the case - the current price is actually at a discount to current NAV (-10.7%), consistent with the Analysis JSON's own -11% to -13% figures - and (b) the model then projects that NAV itself to keep drifting down at the base-case rate (-1.8% p.a.) before applying a further -9% exit discount, i.e. the base case is not claiming the market is mispricing today's NAV, but that today's NAV (and the discount to it) will not be a great combination to hold given the distribution-funded erosion and fee drag already embedded in the trend. This is a legitimate, evidence-based negative view, not a sanity-check failure, and is reported as such rather than smoothed toward a positive number.

sensitivity.methodology: 5-year IRR-build fair value (PV of distributions + PV of exit value at year-5 NAV x column exit discount, both discounted at the row cost of equity), holding the base-case NAV growth path (-1.8% p.a.) and 8% distribution yield constant.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Standard 25/50/25 weighting. Base case is the direct evidence-led continuation of the manager's recent (2-period) underperformance record and the long-standing distribution policy; bull requires a demonstrated alpha turnaround that has not yet occurred; bear is a continuation/worsening of the H1 FY2026 experience, which is a live and recent (not hypothetical) data point.

verdict: At $0.48, Barramundi trades at an approximately -10.7% discount to its current (late-Jul-2026) NAV of $0.5375, consistent with the Analysis JSON's own disclosed -11% to -13% range. This is a genuine income-plus-discount-closing vehicle, not a growth compounder: the 8% p.a. distribution policy is substantially a return of shareholders' own capital rather than organic income (the portfolio's underlying dividend yield is only ~2%), and NAV per share has fallen from $0.71 (FY2018) to ~$0.54 today despite a generally rising Australian equity market over that period - clear evidence that fees plus the distribution policy have exceeded the portfolio's organic total return over a full cycle. Discounting a base-case combination of a continuing mild NAV-per-share decline (-1.8% p.a., reflecting persisting-but-partial manager underperformance, a ~1% management fee, ongoing warrant-dilution drag, and the unchanged 8% distribution) plus a modest narrowing of the exit discount (to -9% from today's -11% to -13%) at a 12% cost of equity produces a base-case intrinsic value of $0.40 (-16.2%) and a probability-weighted intrinsic value of $0.40 (-16.0%). This is reported honestly as a negative-expected-return conclusion at the current price, not adjusted toward a more palatable number - the discount at which BRM currently trades does not appear to be excessive once the demonstrated fee/underperformance drag and distribution-funded NAV erosion are correctly priced in. The warrant tranche that expired 7-Aug-2026 (85.2m units, $0.70 strike) has lapsed with zero dilutive effect given NAV never approached the strike; investors should nonetheless expect a further, similarly structured warrant issue within the next 1-2 years per Barramundi's recurring capital-management pattern, a modest ongoing dilution risk already reflected in the base-case NAV growth build.
